messages.subject: Error in the Cox model
parts:
I have tried to fit a Cox model using the attached data and I get a convergence error and INLA stopped working. The following is the code I used, I tried to fit with or without the cutpoints and I get the same error.
Is there something particular about the attached data that cannot be fit in INLA? I ran the same model with a different data generated from a Weibull distribution and it worked with that data.
Thank you,
Georgiana

cutpoints = c(1,4.33,26)
#fit Cox model in INLA and get estimated survival
formula = inla.surv(t, occ) ~ period
resultcox = inla(formula, family = "coxph", data = sim.data)
resultcox = inla(formula, family = "coxph", data = sim.data, control.hazard=list(model="rw1",cutpoints=cutpoints))

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Error in the Cox model
parts:
On Wed, 2012-07-11 at 07:54 -0700, georgianao wrote:
> I have tried to fit a Cox model using the attached data and I get a
> convergence error and INLA stopped working. The following is the code
> I used, I tried to fit with or without the cutpoints and I get the
> same error.
> Is there something particular about the attached data that cannot be
> fit in INLA? I ran the same model with a different data generated from
> a Weibull distribution and it worked with that data.
> Thank you,
> Georgiana
>
> cutpoints = c(1,4.33,26)
> #fit Cox model in INLA and get estimated survival
> formula = inla.surv(t, occ) ~ period
> resultcox = inla(formula, family = "coxph", data = sim.data)
> resultcox = inla(formula, family = "coxph", data = sim.data,
> control.hazard=list(model="rw1",cutpoints=cutpoints))

you'll need here to put a proper prior on the intercept as it interacts
with the rw-model for the baseline harazard (although its constrained to
sum to zero). default is prec.intercept = 0, which can cause trouble
sometimes.

here is the updated example. I also disovered a minor error in the plot
due to a previous name-change, which I have fixed, so you need to do

inla.upgrade(testing=TRUE)

first, before plotting the results.

***************


sim.data = read.csv("data.csv")

## cutpoints need to cover the range of the data
cutpoints = c(0, 1, 4.33, 26, 53)

resultcox = inla(formula, family = "coxph", data = sim.data, verbose=T,
control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.001))

control.fixed = list(prec.intercept = 0.001),
control.hazard=list(model="rw1",cutpoints=cutpoints))
